title: Tottenham Hotspur — Premier League club content (2026/27)
source: FICTIONAL. Written by the REROUTE team for the hackathon demo, modelled on common football club-content practice: club-owned social channels, a home-market window for full-match recordings, no match broadcast footage in advertising, a club group image-rights pool, partner exclusivity and stadium conditions of entry. No Tottenham Hotspur, Premier League, player or sponsor agreement was supplied or consulted.
disclaimer: FICTIONAL DEMO POLICY — not an actual club, league, player or sponsor agreement. DEMO POLICY — NOT VERIFIED LEGAL CLEARANCE.

provenance.description: Club-produced footage filed in the club's ScorePlay workspace and tagged "partner content"

rules.explanation: Premier League 2026/27 footage is covered by the club's content licence.
Allowed only on the club's own Instagram, Facebook, X, TikTok and YouTube accounts.
Club content is licensed for GB, IE, US, CA, AU and NZ. Other countries belong to international media partners.
Full-match recordings can only be shown in the UK and Ireland (GB, IE) — they come from the live broadcast feed.
Allowed for editorial, organic, sponsored and sales posts, as long as the people and brand rules are met.
Broadcast highlights and full matches can't be used to sell merchandise or tickets — editorial and club social only.
The licence runs for the 2026/27 season: 1 Jul 2026 to 30 Jun 2027.
Players, staff and fans in match-day footage can appear in editorial and organic club posts.
Sponsored and sales posts can show Tottenham's own first-team squad and staff — only if ScorePlay lists them in the squad.
Crowd and stadium shots can be used in sales posts (stadium conditions of entry) when no player is identifiable.
Kit branding and stadium boards that appear incidentally are fine in editorial and organic posts.
Sponsored and sales posts can show the club's own marks and official partners AIA and Nike.
Sales and sponsored posts can’t show other brands — our official partners have exclusivity.
